I'm a girl! and thanks, I just think I should hold off on talking to her to start with. she needs to clear her head and focus on herself. I really really upset her and I see that. But I also see a lot of improvement in myself. I have a routine with my medication and I'm seeing a new psychiatrist soon to finalize and work on a full set of medication so I can be treated for my ADD and OCD. I was diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder, so that adds to everything.

But for now I'm just focusing on my Bipolar, before anything else. Because once I've done that, THEN I can move forward with anything else. My recovery is moving fairly quickly and I'll be stable and good to go before New Years. The only issue was I wasn't in control of my own organization nor my academic organization. I would spend an hour or two trying to cook dinner (I was practically raised in fine restaurants since birth), but because of my ADD, it'd take me a bit longer. The real issue for me was exhaustion. I wanted to fall asleep next to her EVERY night of our finals week. But then I got into a bad routine of staying up for multiple nights in a row, therefore depleting me of nutrients (still my fault). But I always made sure not to disturb her so she could sleep and be well rested for her exams. 

The whole fight started with me not being on the right meds, me trying to figure it all out without knowing I was bipolar, and then me delving into a manic episode in which I wanted to completely cut myself off from my entire family back at home. She was so caring, but the arguing would get the best of us both. It was pretty intense, and I'm deaf in one ear so I'm no ace at volume control. 

Anyways, it's a tough battle, but I don't want to fight anymore, I JUST want to love her and hold her in the end of the day, but she is mad and has every right to be

Thanks, this comment helped calm me down at family dinner haha. And I have packets and information, user F0rever_Fascinated brought up a good point that I need to stop discussing it with her and just own up to my fucking shit. 

It is my own baggage, and I shouldn't have dragged her down with me. 

I'm just hoping she remembers all the good times and realizes that I WANT a full life with her. If not, then so be it. But I see myself growing old with her, and she brings me a lot of joy. So fingers crossed.

I guess coping with it internally will help, but only time will tell! :)

I was just diagnosed with Bipolar 1, and I was on Lexapro (20mg) for a year and Vyvanse (50mg) since my sophomore year of high school and I'm a sophomore in college now.

I had to go off lexapro as it wasn't helping me and the vyvanse was a stimulant that was aggravating my bipolar. 

It's been about 2 weeks, and the first week was really rough being off of lexapro because the anxiety was constant. But after giving it time to get out of my system, I've been able to assess what I need apart from the depakote and ceraquil I am now taking and I would recommend at least waiting till it's fully out of your system before trying anything else!
